tool_input.command:
t=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$t/dest"
# help exits 0
bash rotate.sh --help >/dev/null; echo "rotate --help rc=$?"
bash verify.sh --help >/dev/null; echo "verify --help rc=$?"
# --keep validation
bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name d --keep abc 2>&1 | tail -1; 
# dry run + sidecar removal with 3 archives, keep 2
for s in 20260101-000000 20260102-000000 20260103-000000; do : > "$t/dest/d-$s.tar.gz"; : > "$t/dest/d-$s.tar.gz.sha256"; done
bash rotate.sh --quiet --dry-run --dest "$t/dest" --name d --keep 2
bash rotate.sh --quiet -n --dest "$t/dest" --name d -k 2 2>&1 | tail -1
bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name d --keep=2
echo "remaining:"; ls "$t/dest"
# verify: name filter, missing dir exit 2, unknown option exit 1
bash verify.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name d; echo "verify rc=$?"
bash rotate.sh --quiet --dest "$t/nodir" --name d; echo "missing dest rc=$?"
bash verify.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --bogus 2>&1 | tail -1
# verify: empty sidecar is malformed, name with spaces + BAD
printf '' > "$t/dest/empty.tar.gz.sha256"
bash verify.sh --quiet --dest "$t/dest" --name empty; echo "empty sidecar rc=$?"
rm -rf "$t"

tool_input.description: Syntax-check all scripts and show git status

result:
All checks pass. Summary of the work:

**Bug 1 — `rotate.sh --keep N`** (`rotate.sh:141-149`): the guard used `-lt` (so exactly N backups fell through to deletion) and `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on a list sorted oldest-first, which selected from the KEEP-th line to the *end* — i.e. the newest entries. Now the guard is `-le` and surplus is the oldest `total - keep` entries via `head -n`.

**Bug 2 — `verify.sh` and spaces** (`verify.sh:149-153`): the sidecar line was split with `awk '{print $2}'`, which truncated `my backup-….tar.gz` at the first space, so the name looked missing → BAD. It now uses `read -r expected file <<< "$line"`, which puts the whole remainder (spaces included) into the filename; the digest comparison also switched from unquoted `[ $expected == $actual ]` to quoted `[[ ]]`.

**Refactor**: added `lib/common.sh` containing the shared option-parsing block (`DEST/NAME/KEEP/QUIET/DRY_RUN/ARGS`, `is_uint`, `need_value`, the flag loop wrapped as `parse_common_options`, the `--keep` validation) and the `resolve_dir` helper, with a double-source guard like `lib/log.sh`. `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh` source it and call `parse_common_options "$@"` after defining `usage`/`parse_local_option`, so all flags (`--dest`, `--name`, `--keep`, `--dry-run`, `--quiet`, `--help`, `--`, unknown-option handling) behave identically — verified by hand for help, `--keep=2`, dry-run, sidecar removal, name filter, missing-dest rc=2, and malformed sidecars. `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh`, `lib/log.sh` are untouched.

Test suite (`bash tests/run_tests.sh`): 10/10 ok, including the new regression tests — "verify accepts spaces in an archive name", "rotate deletes nothing when exactly --keep archives exist", "rotate --keep 2 of three deletes the oldest", "rotate keeps the newest --keep archives".

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh` modified; `lib/common.sh` added.
